en-US.author: Kenneth Skovhede
en-US.description: Duplicati is a free, open source, backup client that securely stores encrypted, incremental, compressed backups on cloud storage services and remote file servers.
en-US.name: Duplicati 2
en-US.releaseNotes:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.
Timeouts with remote sources and slow destinations
When a backup reads from a remote source, such as an SMB share or a cloud drive, that is faster than the destination, the reads are paused while a volume is uploaded. The timeout kept counting during these pauses and could fail the transfer although the remote service was responding. The timeout for almost all backends now only counts the time spent waiting for the remote service, not the time Duplicati itself is busy. The SMB backend got the same treatment directly, as it controls the flow itself.
A related problem made SMB and some other backends report incomplete data as a successful backup: when a stalled read hit the inactivity timeout, the timeout handler closed the stream, which took the error away. The error is now kept. SMB delete and rename also failed silently on an unexpected return code, which is now reported.
More timeout fixes:
- The Azure Blob backend set up its timeout stream but did not use it, so timeouts were ignored.
- The SMB client used the library default of 5 seconds when writing chunks to the destination. It now uses --read-write-timeout, which defaults to 30 seconds.
- --list-timeout was not applied to SFTP and MinIO listings, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- Storj transfers that stopped moving were waited for forever. They now fail when no bytes have moved for --read-write-timeout, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A timeout in a synchronous operation did not return when the task was cancelled, which could leave tasks stuck.
- A cancellation by the caller was reported as a timeout, and a timeout could escape as a cancellation, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Resuming remote source reads
A file read from a remote source is now wrapped in a resuming stream. If the connection is lost while reading, the stream reconnects and continues from where it stopped. The data up to that point is read again and hashed, to make sure the file did not change in the meantime. A backend interface for resuming with a range request was added, so backends that support it can resume without re-reading, but no backend implements it yet.
A remote source that dropped or truncated a file used to have the partial file stored as if it was complete. Truncated files are now rejected with a warning and not stored.

Source folders that cannot be read
A source folder that exists but cannot be listed, for example on a failed drive, only gave a warning. The backup then stored a version without any of its files, and the retention policy could remove the versions that still had them. The backup is now stopped, as for a missing source, unless --allow-missing-source is set, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
A backup that was stopped before it started processing files uploaded an empty version as the latest, and warned that the source was likely misconfigured. No version is created now, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
Placeholder files from a sync tool, such as OneDrive, Dropbox or Google Drive, and files moved to offline storage fail to read with a generic error. These errors are now recognized and reported with a message that points to --exclude-non-local-files.

Dry run no longer changes the database
A backup with --dry-run did not touch the remote data, but the compact step committed its decision to the local database. On the next real run, the recorded decision was carried out and files were deleted. The dry run no longer updates the database.

Database downgrade scripts stored in the database
Until now, downgrading a local database required the downgrade script shipped with the newer version, so the downgrade had to be done before uninstalling it. The upgrade and downgrade scripts are now stored in the databases themselves, in a new SchemaScript table. From this release on, the bundled duplicati-database-tool can downgrade a database written by a newer version by using the scripts stored in the database, even if the tool does not know that schema. Downgrades are still started manually. The schema version is not changed by this release.
The default for duplicati-database-tool downgrade is now the newest version the tool itself supports, so a downgrade from the next version needs no explicit version. Downgrading over several versions requires the target version to be given. The tool also no longer mistakes a local database with an index or view named Schedule for a server database, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Restore fixes
- A block that could not be read from its volume stopped the whole restore. Only the files that use the block are now reported as failed, and the other files are restored, thanks @JamBalaya56562. When the database places a block in a volume that does not hold it, the error now names the block instead of failing with a null reference.
- A restore that could not restore some files exited with code 0. It now exits with code 3, as a backup that finished with errors does, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- When a priority file, such as the disk layout of a disk image, fails, the error now says that the restore was stopped because of it and names the file, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- With --restore-symlink-metadata, the extended attributes and the read-only attribute of a symbolic link were applied to the file it points to, also when that file is outside the restore folder. The extended attributes are now set on the link itself, and the attributes are skipped for links, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- On Linux, restoring the creation time overwrote the last write time that had just been restored, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The legacy restore engine did not count restored symbolic links, so restoring only a link ended with a warning that nothing was restored, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Repair and dlist files
Three problems with the names and times of dlist files were fixed, thanks @JamBalaya56562:
- A dlist upload that fails is retried under a name one second later. Backups, synthetic filelists and purges did not record the fileset time in the file, so after a recreate such a version was one second late. The time is now recorded in every dlist file.
- A retried dlist upload after a repair or purge left a placeholder version dated 1970-01-01 in the version list until the next backup, and restoring that version failed.
- Repairing a missing dlist file gave the replacement a name at least one second after the original, which could put it after a newer version. The file is now uploaded again under its own name, and the search for a free name stops after the configured number of tries.

Recovery tool
The recovery tool can now add encryption to a backup that was made without encryption, with the new --add-encryption option.
Recompressing to the same format uploaded the new file over the original name, and the following delete removed it, emptying the destination. Files that keep their name are now left in place, and --reencrypt warns when the files are not encrypted, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Reporting
Thanks @JamBalaya56562 for a series of fixes to the report modules:
- Values put into report templates were used as a regex replacement string, so a file name or option value containing $ sequences corrupted the report body. The keys were also expanded in several passes over the already inserted values, so text such as %backup-name% inside a log line was expanded too, and a key with regex characters stopped the report. Values are now inserted literally and keys are expanded once.
- A failing HTTP report, status report or XMPP target skipped the remaining targets. Each target is now tried on its own.
- A report that failed to send made the operation a warning, but the job log did not show why. The stored result now includes the warnings and errors logged after it was written.
- A failing --run-script-before script or an option that failed validation stopped the operation before the report modules were set up, so no report was sent.
- The command line printed "Backup completed successfully!" also when a script stopped the backup or it ended with errors.
- A compact that changed something was logged twice in the job log, and the database was vacuumed twice.
The Reason field of restore test reports is now passed on in reduced reporting mode.

Storage providers
- Google Workspace files were read fully into memory before being backed up, which used a lot of memory and failed for files above 2 GB. The data is now streamed in chunks, and the same approach is applied to Microsoft 365. The Google Workspace module also follows the standard timeout options, and chat attachments are stored with their content instead of their metadata.
- The progress bar during a Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace delta walk often jumped from 0 to 100%. The walk now reports its progress as it goes.
- Google answers both a missing permission and a rate limit with 403, and the error body that tells them apart was dropped. Google Drive and Google Cloud Storage now report Google's reason, and rate limits are retried with backoff, also for the chunks of a resumable upload, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A Google Drive upload that timed out on the client could still be completed by Drive, leaving a second copy that a delete did not remove. All copies of the name are now deleted, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The B2 retry logic now follows the B2 guidelines, and a bug that could truncate listings was fixed.
- SMB left file handles open on the server when a get, delete or rename failed, and a failed close replaced the listing error with "Not enough credits", thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The SharePoint v2 backend required --site-id and never looked the site up from the URL. The site is now found from the URL, and a --site-id that names another site is reported as a conflict, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Server and user interface
